releases.title: Co-Adaptive Assistance and Governed Desktop Agency
releases.summary: Consented assistance co-adaptation, accessibility-grounded desktop control, durable and scheduled autonomy, MCP tools, voice-first control while working, and fail-closed settings and approvals

features.name: Assistance Co-Adaptation
features.description: An opt-in, consented selection study models how a person, the interface and Heliox adapt to each other and predicts which help suits this person today (a larger target, a confirm step, a clarifying question or another input) within rules the person sets. It changes presentation only, never commits an ambiguous selection by guessing, and every published result so far comes from simulated users.

features.name: Accessibility-Grounded Desktop Control
features.description: Desktop clicks are grounded in the accessibility tree instead of pixels, buttons can be pressed in the background without moving the cursor, browser actions use page snapshots, and the person can take the desktop back at any time while Heliox can hand it over when it needs help. No virtual machine is involved.

features.name: Durable and Scheduled Autonomy
features.description: Autonomous jobs survive daemon restarts and resume only when the person asks, scheduled runs are limited to an approved list of actions, unreachable goals are reported instead of faked, and each tool call of background work appears as a card in chat.

features.name: Tools from Your MCP Servers
features.description: Heliox can call tools from the person's own MCP servers listed in mcp_servers.json. Read-only tools run directly, every other tool asks first, and Settings shows each server with a reload button.

features.name: Voice-First Control While Heliox Works
features.description: Speaking while a task runs does what the person means: corrections, questions and a spoken no reach the running task, background approval dialogs stay open while the person keeps working, and the approval dialog shows what an action will actually run. The world model reviews every autonomous plan.

features.name: Fail-Closed Settings and Approvals
features.description: Settings change safely while work runs and survive unreadable or hand-edited config files; an action family a gateway profile does not list is read-only; an approval that is never answered expires instead of running; a plan resumed after a restart runs only the ticked actions; and a gesture can approve only a dialog the person can see.

releases.title: Verified Autonomy and Runtime Hardening
releases.summary: Truthful outcomes, transactional settings, authenticated collaboration, coordinated multimodal control, bounded resources, and measured execution quality

features.name: Truthful Execution Contracts
features.description: Completed work is revalidated against executor and checkpoint contracts, while failed, rejected, skipped, partial, and unavailable paths remain visible instead of being reported as successful.

features.name: Transactional Live Settings
features.description: Runtime configuration changes are validated and applied atomically, roll back on failure, and can update supported model limits, devices, calendars, camera, gesture, voice, and mesh controls without leaving split state.

features.name: Authenticated Peer Collaboration
features.description: Opt-in LAN peers use authenticated setup, bounded timeouts, constrained delegation, and the same permission and startup gates as local collaboration.

features.name: Coordinated Multimodal Control
features.description: Voice, gesture, gaze, cursor, approval, and staged neural inputs arbitrate shared resources more reliably, including camera ownership, gesture priority, and neural-sidecar diagnostics.

features.name: Bounded Runtime Resources
features.description: Daemon shutdown now quiesces autonomous jobs, monitors, browser resources, subscription CLIs, input services, and collaboration work; idle local TTS and model workers release heavy memory outside the long-lived daemon.

features.name: Measured Execution Quality
features.description: The executor records step-budget quality, skips actions only when deterministic postconditions are already satisfied, preserves fast local status paths, and publishes a refreshed reproducible benchmark bundle.

releases.title: Governed Intelligence and Handoff
releases.summary: Subscription-backed planning, local MCP, secure Air Handoff, verified integrations, and one governed cognitive runtime

features.name: Existing AI Subscription Providers
features.description: Use an existing Codex or Claude Code login through the provider's official CLI, choose an available model, and inspect bounded plan-usage evidence without copying OAuth credentials into Heliox.

features.name: Local Heliox MCP
features.description: IDE agents can stage Heliox tasks through a local MCP server while the Heliox daemon retains identity checks, permission gates, approvals, and execution.

features.name: Secure Air Handoff
features.description: Cast a deliberately selected Heliox view to a paired mobile browser over an ephemeral encrypted session, with explicit start, stop, and gesture controls.

features.name: Verified Integrations
features.description: Email, calendar, and SSH settings now reach their executable specialists through credential-vault, RPC, policy, and result contracts.

features.name: Unified Cognitive Runtime
features.description: Companion narration, learned-risk interruption, follow-up suggestions, and autonomous execution now use the live production gateway instead of duplicate runtime state.

features.name: Evidence-Driven Reliability
features.description: Local health reviews, neural staged-goal dispatch, model timeouts, microphone capture, MCP version reporting, and forensic results now fail more truthfully.

releases.title: Adaptive Companion Release
releases.summary: The complete v0.11 companion feature set with deterministic Windows packaging

features.name: Reliable Windows Release Delivery
features.description: The Windows release pipeline now prefetches and checksum-verifies WiX with explicit retries before building MSI and NSIS installers.

releases.title: Adaptive Multimodal Companion
releases.summary: Adaptive learning, coordinated multimodal control, expanded specialists, and guarded neural research

features.name: Continuous Companion Loop
features.description: Always-on voice, spoken suggestions, interruption, and autonomous browser or application control now share one coordinated execution loop.

features.name: Adaptive Intelligence Stack
features.description: A bounded experience ledger, temporal memory, verified online adaptation, strategy evolution, and an optional JEPA-style predictor advise future plans.

features.name: Expanded Specialist Mesh
features.description: Twenty-one specialists provide concrete coverage for all 156 declared action types across desktop, browser, developer, integration, and research workflows.

features.name: Reliable Multimodal Control
features.description: Gaze, 3D hand gestures, cursor control, wake-word audio, and workflow bindings can operate together with temporal false-positive rejection.

features.name: Guarded Neural Research Pipeline
features.description: Synthetic BrainFlow and recorded EEGBCI paths now exercise calibrated, signed, consent-bounded neural intents without claiming live brain control.

features.name: Truthful Execution and Delivery
features.description: Application launch, browser targeting, approvals, cancellations, result reporting, first-run Chromium setup, and cross-platform packaging are more deterministic.

releases.title: Reliable Interactive Sessions
releases.summary: Persistent sessions, faster browser control, and coordinated companion reliability

features.name: Persistent Private Sessions
features.description: Start isolated chats, reopen prior sessions, and retain adaptive memory without leaking one conversation's transcript into another.

features.name: Faster Semantic Browser Control
features.description: Common browser tasks use bounded planning, resolve controls by meaning, and serialize shared-page actions to avoid slow or conflicting execution.

features.name: Coordinated Companion Services
features.description: Narration, learned-risk interruption, voice, and verified follow-up suggestions remain available together while approvals pass through every action gate.

features.name: Safer, Truthful Task Results
features.description: Cancelled work, cloud-provider failures, destructive file changes, and exact findings now produce bounded, redacted, recoverable results.

releases.title: Interactive Companion and Reliability
releases.summary: Companion intelligence, learned safety, multimodal control, and reliable execution

features.name: Interactive Companion
features.description: Opt-in narration, risk interruption, spoken follow-up, and suggestions now share one coordinated conversation loop.

features.name: Learned Risk World Model
features.description: On-device learned predictions now advise the deterministic safety gate and can add caution or pause risky actions.

features.name: Unified Camera Intelligence
features.description: Gaze, hand gestures, and cursor control can run together from one camera stream without suppressing enabled inputs.

features.name: Moderated Plugin Marketplace
features.description: Reviewed packages are verified by manifest and SHA-256 before installation, and merged catalog entries appear without a desktop release.

features.name: Reliable Approvals and Results
features.description: Approval responses remain live on the active connection, while cancelled, blocked, and failed actions now finish with truthful terminal results.

features.name: Durable Voice and Gesture Workflows
features.description: Multi-step workflows can be submitted, paused, resumed, and inspected while autonomous healing remains separately permission-gated.

releases.title: JARVIS Autonomy
releases.summary: Background autonomy and local multimodal control

features.name: Autonomous Background Tasks
features.description: Run permission-gated multi-step tasks while continuing to use the app.

features.name: Live Execution Narrator
features.description: Optionally hear short progress descriptions and risk interruptions.

features.name: Local Voice, Gesture, and Gaze Inputs
features.description: Use on-device multimodal controls without sending camera frames.
